transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I can’t shake this feeling that I’ve failed my family and that everything that’s gone wrong is my fault. My wife and my cousin strongly urged me to come get some help after I finally broke down and opened up to them recently. I just feel like I've ruined our lives, and I don't know how to fix it.
Can you tell me more about when these feelings of guilt and failure started, was it triggered by a specific event or did they develop over time?

It started about eight months ago after a major argument with my adult daughter about my long work hours and missed family events, which ended with her moving out of state. Since then, I’ve been constantly replaying all my past mistakes in my head. I just feel like I’ve completely failed her and the rest of my family, and I can't let it go.
Have these feelings of guilt and failure been constant over the past eight months, or have they varied in intensity, and how have they affected your daily life and relationships?

Yes, they have been heavy and constant every single day since she left, and it has completely taken over my life. At work, my performance has dropped so much that my manager has pulled me aside twice, and at home, I've let the bills pile up and stopped organizing the family gatherings I used to love. I've mostly just withdrawn from my wife and the rest of the family because I feel so overwhelmed.

Have you experienced any periods over the past eight months where you felt significantly better for a couple of weeks or more, or have these feelings of guilt and failure been consistently present without any notable improvement?

No, there haven't been any breaks or times where I felt better. Every single day since my daughter moved away, this heavy feeling and the guilt have been constantly there without any relief. It just feels like a dark cloud that hasn't lifted for a single day.

You've mentioned these feelings have been constant for eight months without any relief, but can you tell me if there have been any times, even briefly, where your mood or energy levels seemed to improve, or if you've experienced any periods of increased irritability or restlessness?

No, I haven't had any times where my mood or energy improved, and I haven't felt irritable like that either. This heavy, empty feeling and low energy have been completely constant, day in and day out, for the entire eight months since my daughter left. It just never lets up.
Have you experienced any significant weight loss or loss of interest in activities you once enjoyed over the past eight months, and if so, how have these changes affected your daily functioning?

I haven't really noticed any significant weight loss, but I have completely lost interest in things I used to love over the last eight months, like closing sales deals or grilling for my family. It has badly affected my daily life—I've let bills pile up at home, isolated myself from everyone, and my manager has pulled me aside twice because my work performance has dropped so much.

You've had these feelings of guilt and failure for eight months without any relief, but can you tell me if you've had any previous episodes like this in your life, or if this is the first time you've experienced such persistent feelings of sadness and guilt?

No, this is the first time I have ever felt this way. I don't recall ever having any previous episodes of such persistent sadness or guilt in my life before this happened. It's all completely new and overwhelming to me.

Given that this is your first episode of persistent sadness and guilt, and it's lasted for eight months without any significant improvement, can you tell me if you've had any periods of hypomanic or manic episodes in the past, where you felt extremely happy, energetic, or irritable for a period of time?

No, I have never experienced anything like that. I've never had periods of extreme high energy, feeling unusually hyper, or manic episodes in the past. Before these past eight months, my mood was always pretty stable and normal.
Have you experienced any thoughts of hearing voices, seeing things that aren't there, or having beliefs that seem unreal or detached from reality during these past eight months?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. I don't hear voices, see things that aren't there, or hold any unusual beliefs. My mind is clear in that way, it's just very heavy with sadness and guilt.

You mentioned this is your first episode of persistent sadness and guilt, but can you tell me if you've had any previous milder episodes of depression that might have lasted for shorter periods, even if they didn't seem as severe as what you're experiencing now?
No, I don't recall ever having any milder periods of depression or persistent sadness in the past. This entire struggle is completely new to me, and I've never gone through anything like this before.

Given that you've had no previous episodes of depression and this is your first experience with persistent sadness and guilt, do you think you could have had a milder depressive episode in the past that you might not have recognized as depression at the time?

No, I really don't think I've ever gone through anything like this in the past. I've always been highly focused on my work and providing for my family, so this heavy feeling of sadness and guilt is completely new to me.

You've had this episode of depression for eight months without any relief, but looking back, do you think there might have been any shorter periods in your life where you felt somewhat similar, even if not as severe, or is this truly the first and only episode you've experienced?
This is truly the first and only time I have ever felt this way. I have never experienced any period in my life, short or long, that felt anything like what I'm going through now.

You've confirmed this is your first episode of depression, but can you tell me if you're experiencing any significant stressors or life events currently, or if there's anything that might be contributing to the persistence of your feelings of guilt and sadness?

Yes, the biggest thing dragging me down is the major argument I had with my daughter eight months ago about my long work hours and missing family events. She moved out of state right after, and our relationship has been strained with almost no contact since. I just can't get past the guilt of feeling like I've completely failed her as a father.

Given that you've had no previous episodes of depression and this is your first experience with persistent sadness and guilt, do you think the current episode might be related to the significant life event of your daughter moving away, and if so, how do you think your feelings might change if your relationship with her were to improve?

Yes, my depression and guilt definitely started right after that big argument and my daughter's move eight months ago. While I desperately wish things could be better, I feel so overwhelmed by guilt and the belief that I ruined her life by prioritizing work that it's hard to imagine her ever forgiving me, or me ever deserving that forgiveness.

Do you feel like your depression and guilt would significantly improve or resolve if you were able to reconcile with your daughter and improve your relationship with her, or do you think these feelings have become more of a general part of your life regardless of your relationship with her?

Even though the fight with my daughter started this, these feelings have spread to every part of my life now. This heavy, dark cloud doesn't lift whether I'm at work or even holding my grandson on FaceTime. The guilt of feeling like an overall failure as a father and husband has just become a constant, general part of my life.

You've mentioned that these feelings of guilt and failure have been constant for eight months without any relief, but can you tell me if you've noticed any subtle differences in how these feelings affect you from one month to the next, or if they've remained completely unchanged?

No, there haven't been any changes at all from month to month. Ever since my daughter moved away eight months ago, these feelings of guilt and failure have remained completely steady and unchanged. It doesn't fluctuate; it just feels like a constant, heavy weight that hasn't lifted at all.

You've had these persistent feelings of guilt and failure for eight months without any relief, but can you tell me if you've experienced any subtle differences in the intensity or nature of these feelings over time, even if the overall heaviness remains, that might help distinguish this episode from other potential conditions?

There really haven't been any subtle changes or fluctuations in these feelings. The heaviness and guilt have been completely steady and unrelenting for the entire eight months, starting from the moment I wake up and persisting all day. There are simply no periods of relief or variation.

Can you describe how your daily functioning and social interactions have changed since the onset of these feelings, and if there have been any periods where you felt like you were adapting or coping better with your situation?

My daily life has really fallen apart—my work performance has dropped so much that my manager has pulled me aside twice, I've let bills pile up at home, and I've stopped organizing family events, choosing to just keep to myself instead. There haven't been any periods where I felt like I was coping or adapting better; it has just been a steady, continuous struggle for the past eight months since my daughter left.

You've had this episode of depression for eight months without any relief, but looking back, do you feel that the nature of your depressive symptoms has changed or evolved in any way over time, or have they remained consistent in character?

While the heavy, empty feeling has been pretty constant over the last eight months, some aspects have definitely worsened over time. As the months passed without any reconciliation with my daughter, I found myself pulling away from my family even more, my work slipped further, and recently, the thoughts that they might be better off without me have become much more frequent and intense.

You've mentioned that these feelings of guilt and failure have been constant for eight months without any relief, but can you tell me if you've experienced any periods where you felt like you were at a lower point or a higher point in terms of your mood and functioning, even if the overall pattern has been consistent?

No, I haven't experienced any high points or times of relief at all. My mood and functioning have just been steadily and consistently low, like a constant dark cloud or heavy feeling that has stayed with me ever since the fight with my daughter eight months ago.

You've had this episode of depression for eight months without any relief, but can you tell me if you think the persistence of your symptoms, despite their consistency, might suggest a more chronic form of depression, or if you believe there's still a possibility for significant improvement with the right treatment?

I don't really know much about clinical terms like 'chronic depression' or what that means. Right now, I just feel too hopeless and overwhelmed by everything to really know if I can ever get better. It's hard to imagine anything making a difference at this point.

Given that you've had no previous episodes of depression and this is your first experience with persistent sadness and guilt, do you think the fact that your symptoms have lasted for eight months without any relief might indicate a more severe or chronic form of depression, and how does that impact your expectations for recovery?

Yes, it really has been constant for the last eight months without any break. Because it has gone on for so long, it feels deeply ingrained and completely overwhelming. I feel so hopeless about the future and really doubt that I can ever recover or get back to the person I used to be.

Given the duration and consistency of your symptoms, do you think the lack of any periods of significant improvement or relief over the past eight months might suggest that your depression could be a more chronic condition, rather than a single episode?

Yes, it really does feel like a permanent, heavy cloud rather than just a temporary phase. Since the fight with my daughter eight months ago, there hasn't been a single break or good day from this feeling. It honestly feels like this is just how my life is now, and I can't shake it.

Given the chronic nature of your symptoms, do you think that even if your relationship with your daughter were to improve significantly, your feelings of guilt and sadness might still persist, or would you expect them to lift somewhat?

While I desperately wish reconciling with my daughter would fix everything, I honestly fear that this heavy sadness and guilt would still persist. This dark cloud feels constant no matter what is happening, and my guilt goes far beyond just that one fight—I feel like I've fundamentally failed as a father and husband by prioritizing my work over them for so many years.

Do you think that your persistent feelings of guilt and sadness are likely to continue even if you receive treatment and support, or do you believe that with the right help, you could experience significant improvement and potentially return to your previous level of functioning?

I honestly don't know if any treatment or support can help me at this point. I feel so completely hopeless that it's hard to imagine ever getting back to the person I used to be, even with professional help.

Do you think your current feelings of guilt and sadness are more related to the ongoing situation with your daughter, or have they become a more general and persistent part of your life that you don't see changing even if your situation with her improves?

While it all started with my daughter leaving, these feelings have spread to every corner of my life, and this heavy, empty feeling doesn't lift even during moments that should bring joy, like holding my grandson on FaceTime. Because I feel like I have fundamentally failed my family and don't deserve their forgiveness, I really struggle to see things changing even if my relationship with her improved.

Given the duration of your symptoms and their consistent presence without relief, do you think it's possible that your depression might be a single, severe episode that could potentially improve with treatment, or do you believe it has become a more chronic condition?

I'm really not sure about the difference between those medical terms, and I haven't really thought about it in those ways. All I know is that this weight feels so heavy and constant every single day. It has been going on for so long now that it is just very hard to imagine it ever lifting.
Do you think that even with treatment, your feelings of guilt and sadness could potentially improve significantly, or do you believe they have become a permanent part of your life?

I honestly feel like these feelings have become a permanent part of my life, and I can't imagine them ever improving. I've permanently ruined my relationship with my daughter and failed my family so badly that I don't even deserve to get better or find relief.
Do you think that your current episode of depression is more likely a single, severe episode that could improve with time and treatment, or do you feel it has become a chronic part of your life?

I'm really not sure, and I haven't thought about it in those terms. Right now, because of how heavy and hopeless everything feels every single day, it is just very hard to imagine things ever getting better.

Given the options of a single episode of major depressive disorder or recurrent depressive disorder, which one do you think better describes your current situation, considering this is your first episode but it has lasted for eight months without any relief?

Since this is the very first time I have ever felt this way in my life, a "single episode" definitely sounds more accurate. It has just been one continuous, unbroken struggle for the last eight months since the fight with my daughter, without any periods of feeling like my old self.
